parts.ask: 100 bottle volumes x ml coded y = x − 1000, Σy = 847, Σy² = 13 510.09: (i) show that the unbiased estimate of the mean of x is 1008.47; (ii) calculate the unbiased estimate of the variance of x
parts.ms: M1 ȳ = 8.47 (or Σx = 100 847); A1* x̄ = 1000 + 8.47, labelled as the mean of x; M1 (13 510.09 − 100 × 8.47²)/99 (allow for 1064); A1 64 cao, do not isw (MS p.7)
parts.er: Many did not label 1008.47 clearly as x̄ (called it y, or no label); many added 1000 to the variance (1064), not realising Var(X + a) = Var(X) (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Machine set to mean 1010 ml; a 5% test checks whether the mean has changed: write down hypotheses for a 2-tailed test
parts.ms: B1 in terms of μ (μy = 10 form allowed) (MS p.7)
parts.er: Many confused the sample mean 1008.47 with the null value 1010, reversing them or using 1008.47 for both (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the critical region for X̄ in this test
parts.ms: M1 (X̄ − 1010)/(8/√100) = ±z; B1 1.96 (1.6449 if one-tailed in (b)); A1 both limits; A1ft select the two tails as the region, not z values. A region of the form 1008.432 < X̄ < 1011.568 is penalised (SC) (MS pp.7–8)
parts.er: Weak understanding of critical regions: most found the limits but gave a confidence-interval-style answer; some computed a z-score or p-value instead of the requested critical region and lost credit (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Using (a) and (c), comment on whether the machine needs to be stopped and reset, with a reason
parts.final_form: 1008.47 not in the CR, so no need to stop/reset
parts.ms: M1 compare 1008.47 with their CR (CR must be clear); A1ft consistent conclusion; SC M0A1 for a CR between the limits and "no need to reset" (MS pp.7–8)
parts.er: Same confusion between the critical region for X̄ and a confidence interval (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Explain why using σ² = s² is reasonable here
parts.ms: B1 the sample is large (n = 100) (MS p.8)
parts.er: Well answered; most were well rehearsed (ER p.3)
